usage: - A countable noun in written and spoken Cantonese, but it is more often used as a specific plant name than as a general everyday noun.
- Common in nature, gardening, and religious contexts; it often refers to the flower itself, not the whole plant.
- Can appear alone or in compounds and set phrases, especially when talking about ponds, temples, or summer scenery.
- Neutral and natural in standard Cantonese; for everyday conversation, people may also say 荷花 in some contexts, depending on the exact plant being described.
